methodNotes.title: Whole-sign versus equal houses: different origins
methodNotes.text: Whole-sign houses assign the entire zodiac sign containing the Ascendant to house one: its cusp is 0° of that sign. Equal houses from the Ascendant divide the ecliptic into twelve 30° houses beginning at the actual Ascendant degree. For a synthetic Ascendant of 18° Taurus, whole-sign house one starts at 0° Taurus, while equal house one starts at 18° Taurus. The sky positions do not change when the house convention changes; a planet near a boundary can change house. This is a method definition and synthetic illustration, not an external worked birth example.
limitations: Not every system called equal houses uses the Ascendant; name the variant explicitly.
A house-placement disagreement does not by itself establish that either interpretation predicts an outcome.

methodNotes.title: Placidus: time arcs and high-latitude limits
methodNotes.text: Placidus houses divide semidiurnal and seminocturnal arcs: the arcs of apparent daily motion from horizon to meridian above and below the horizon. Its intermediate cusps are ecliptic points satisfying the specified fractions of their own arcs. It is not simply twelve equal zodiac sectors or a trisection of an ecliptic quadrant. Latitude and local time matter. In polar situations the required rising or setting geometry may be absent; a fallback system must be labelled rather than silently called Placidus.
limitations: Definition checked in the maintainer technical manual; second independent publisher retrieval was unsuccessful.
Software parity and the interpretation of a house require separate evidence.

methodNotes.title: Tropical versus sidereal: origin, stars and precession
methodNotes.locator: Swiss Ephemeris general documentation §2.8.1; Rao §1.3.13,printed p.18
methodNotes.text: The tropical zodiac sets 0° Aries at the vernal equinox on the ecliptic. A sidereal zodiac selects its origin relative to a stellar reference; different ayanamsha conventions choose different offsets. Precession changes the equinox relative to the stars, so tropical and sidereal longitude labels slowly diverge. In the usual offset method, sidereal longitude equals tropical longitude minus the chosen ayanamsha, normalized to 0–360°. This is not a fixed celestial-equator reference, and neither zodiac is identical to the unequal modern IAU constellation boundaries. The same observed planet may have different sign labels without the planet moving.
limitations: The app uses a named linear Lahiri approximation, not exact universal sidereal or JHora parity.
A frame difference is not evidence for different physical influences.

A matching date or angle validates that field only. Shared Moon/Sun inputs do not make two symbolic methods independent evidence. Do not infer diagnosis, guaranteed fortune, war, disasters or a person’s beliefs from the reading.

Use practical evidence for consequential decisions.
